description: The Rasmussen family's own home on Collingwood Street in Vancouver — designed and built by Søren for his family, and the project closest to home in every sense. As the Rasmussen Residence, the house received a Georgie Award in 1999.

The firm's portfolio described it as drawing inspiration from the early Arts and Crafts style, detailed with the sense of craftsmanship of Vancouver's early houses: an entry planned to soften the garage and give way to a large copper beech tree, and living floors gathered under a large, enveloping roof whose extended eaves shade the decks and terraces.

Behind the house, the garden is made with the same care as the architecture: a glass-roofed timber pergola on cast concrete columns, a koi pond crossed by a low wooden deck, and a landscape of lawn, Japanese maple, stone path and clipped evergreen hedge.
note: The original site's Collingwood Residence gallery was not archived; more photographs to come from the family archive.
